name: Library TV
overview: Always-on channels from your own libraries
description: Experimental virtual television with persistent episode order, time blocks, automatic library channels, and commercial breaks. No idle encoding: H.264/AAC files play directly, and only other formats are encoded while watched.

versions.changelog:
Captions for Live TV channels.

- Each channel has a Captions setting: Off (default), Forced only (foreign-language dialogue), or On when the program has captions, plus an optional caption language (English, en or eng).
- Captions come from subtitle tracks in the file or subtitle files beside it (such as Episode.en.srt). Full captions, then SDH/closed captions, then the default track are preferred.
- Live TV streams can't carry subtitle tracks, so captions are drawn into the picture: they work in every app, everyone watching the channel sees them, and programs with captions are encoded while they play (up to 720p). Duplicate a channel to offer it with and without captions.
- Captions stay in sync after commercial breaks and when tuning in part-way through.
- Embedded CEA-608/708 closed captions are not supported.

Less freezing, and more accurate commercials and bumpers.

- Programs run about three seconds ahead of the clock: the plugin paces the stream from its own timestamps, so the next program, bumper or commercial starts while the player still has seconds buffered. Works on every FFmpeg version.
- Copied video resuming after a break starts on a keyframe, so timestamps never run backwards.
- Far less encoding: only pictures more than 8% off the channel's shape are corrected (1.85:1 films and widescreen DVDs now play directly), at no more than 720p. Channel health warns if encoding can't keep up.
- Studios containing a network name count as that network ("Nickelodeon Animation Studio", "Cartoon Network Studios"), and nicknames work: Nick, CN, Williams Street.
- Commercials and bumpers named after a show or movie play only with that show.
- When no clip suits a program, its breaks are left out instead of using another network's clips.
- Guide preview shows why each commercial and bumper was chosen, and labels bumpers.

Bumpers, commercial breaks during shows and movies, a shared commercial library sorted automatically by file name, and no more stretched pictures between programs.

- Bumpers: one plays going into and coming out of each commercial break (one between programs on channels without commercials), matched by network and decade like commercials.
- Commercial breaks during programs: one per episode and two per movie by default (0-5 each), placed at chapter marks when the file has them. A break still follows every program, and the Live TV guide lists each program once.
- Shared commercial library: choose commercials and bumpers once for every channel. After startup and at each refresh, every file and folder name is read for a year ('94, 1994), decade (90s, 1990s) and network, and each clip is sorted to the programs that match it. Works on channels that mix several networks.
- Picture shape per channel (16:9 by default, or 4:3): programs in another shape are encoded with black bars so Jellyfin never stretches them. Or choose "Each program's own shape, restarting players" to play every program in its own shape and restart the apps watching when the shape changes.
- A missing program skips its remaining parts in one step.

Commercials match the network and era of the program they follow, shows always continue to their next episode on a channel, and channels encode only when needed and recover from stalls.

- Commercials filed in network folders (Adult Swim, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, Toonami...) follow programs from that network, chosen by a time block or channel setting, the show's tags, then its studio. Programs from other networks get only commercials outside network folders.
- Commercials come from the program's decade, or the nearest one available. Name commercial folders or files with a year or decade, such as 1980s or Cola (1985).
- Content restrictions keep genres or tags, such as Horror, off the air during set hours on every channel.
- A show continues from the last episode its channel aired, even when it is in both the default lineup and a time block. The same show in two libraries counts once, and duplicate episodes air once.
- H.264 files with stereo AAC audio play directly. Only other formats are encoded, so every program reaches Jellyfin in the same formats. Always encode replaces Compatibility encoding; existing channels switch to the new behavior.
- Stalled playback restarts automatically without disconnecting viewers, a file that ends early starts the next program at once, and short gaps keep the connection alive.
- Rebuilding future slots keeps the current program's commercial break.

Rotate between shows with a configurable episodes-in-a-row setting

- Pools now air "Episodes in a row" episodes of one series (2 by default) before the next series takes a turn, spreading each series evenly through the cycle. Movies take one turn each and every item still airs once per cycle. Set it to 0 to keep the previous straight-through order. Existing rotations are reordered once and keep their place.
- Daily limits keep their quotas on servers with non-Gregorian locales.
- The guide still reaches the current time after long downtime.
- Joining a channel while its stream is stopping now starts a fresh stream.
- Malformed saved settings return 400, and unplayable channels return 503, instead of unhandled errors.
- Jellyfin's Refresh Guide task is queued once after recovery shifts program times.
- Library refreshes check each media folder once instead of per file.

Request three seconds of live input analysis for Library TV folder and Live TV playback, overriding the long server fallback that can delay channel tuning. Includes all 0.4.0 features. Actual startup time also depends on media, storage and client buffering.

Consolidated update: bounded missing-media recovery, hardened FFmpeg cleanup, safe future-slot rebuilding, private-token-free settings backup/restore, detailed channel diagnostics, guide size limits, and real transport tests. Includes all previous builder, numbering and deferred-startup improvements.

Defers schedule work and Plugin Pages registration until the host has started, Jellyfin core startup has completed, and a shared 30-second settling period has elapsed. Heavy service resolution is lazy; startup requests report waiting and the builder offers retry.

Custom manual and automatic channel numbers and names, subchannel sorting and conflict checks, stable automatic assignments, progress retention for disabled channels, on-demand schedule health, bounded guide previews, and per-refresh query reuse.

Visual channel builder with searchable show/movie selection, time blocks, commercial folders, guide preview, and optional Plugin Pages 3+ integration. Existing channel IDs and saved rotations are preserved.
Adds a separate Library TV home folder containing playable channels. Uses the same schedules and shared streams as Live TV. Experimental; validate playback transitions on your clients.
Initial experimental release. Validate channel transitions on your clients before relying on unattended playback.
